transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Karen Wu (HarborLight - Head of InfoSec), Miguel Santos (HarborLight - Cloud Architect), Priya Nair (HarborLight - App Owner)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Weekly security check-in for POC. Covered SSO/SAML integration timeline, audit log export/retention options during pilot, SOC2 evidence requests, KMS/encryption approach, and next steps for technical validation.

Topics: SSO, Audit Logs, Data Retention, SOC2, VPC/KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Karen: Hey, Karen here.
[00:14] Miguel: Miguel on my side.
[00:16] Priya: Priya.
[00:18] Maya: Great, Jonah and I from Redwood, we're just going to pick up where we left off on the security items.
[00:30] Jonah: Yeah, mainly SSO, audit logs, retention windows - and then SOC two, I mean SOC 2 evidence requests.
[00:40] Karen: Sock two, yes. And just to flag we have a couple people out this week so if we miss a detail we'll loop them in.
[00:50] Maya: Totally understandable. First item, SSO. Miguel, you were going to test the SAML metadata we sent?
[01:05] Miguel: I tried to import the metadata, but our test IdP complained about the ACS URL. The metadata had the callback on the api endpoint, I think the environment suffix was wrong.
[01:20] Jonah: Ahh yeah, that's likely the staging vs prod mismatch. We'll send you an environment-specific metadata file. Might be the relay state too.
[01:30] Priya: Quick Q, during the POC will we have users provisioned via SSO or are we using invite-only accounts?
[01:40] Maya: Good question - for the pilot we typically do SSO for a subset of users and invite links for devs. That said, if you want full SSO flow, we can enable it but there may be a short handshake to align metadata.
[01:55] Karen: We prefer SSO for compliance reasons; we want SAML assertions in the audit trail so we can tie actions to internal IDs.
[02:10] Jonah: We record the authenticated user id in request logs; the SAML nameID maps to user_id. We'll include that in the audit schema we share.
[02:20] Miguel: That leads into audit logs - what format do they come in and how long are they stored during the POC?
[02:35] Jonah: By default the hosted logs are retained 90 days, but for POC we can make a copy exported to your S3 or SIEM with configurable retention. The log payload includes timestamp, request id, user id, model, route, response size, and an event type.
[02:50] Karen: We need to validate that the logs include the SAML nameID and the resource identifiers - and redact any PII from prompt text.
[03:05] Jonah: Prompt redaction: we have options - either redact on ingestion or provide truncated prompt hashes. For pilot we'd recommend redaction on our side, plus you pulling raw logs into your SIEM if you want to run the evals.
[03:20] Priya: On redaction, will that interfere with quality tuning? We need some prompt context to tune prompts.
[03:30] Jonah: Right, so we can provide a schema where we store a hashed prompt plus a minimal unredacted snippet under an encrypted field accessible only to your team - requires KMS-backed keys.
[03:45] Miguel: Speaking of KMS, can we bring our own keys? We prefer customer-managed keys in our KMS/HSM for sensitive workloads.
[03:58] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports BYOK in the private deployment. For hosted POC we can integrate with your cloud KMS via a cross-account CMK for encryption-at-rest of logs and artifacts. We will send the KMS integration guide.
[04:15] Karen: Is there an audit trail of key usage? We need key access logs for our auditors.
[04:25] Jonah: Key usage is surfaced via the cloud provider's KMS audit logs - we can provide instructions to link those into your centralized logging.
[04:35] Priya: SOC2 - we saw the SOC 2 report you shared, but we have a couple of detailed control questions around change management and access reviews during closed pilot.
[04:50] Maya: Sure. We are SOC 2 Type II and can provide the report plus the SOC 2 bridge letter for the pilot period. For change management, we maintain documented processes and can provide evidence samples.
[05:05] Karen: We need to confirm the scope - does the SOC2 cover the private deployment controls if we go to VPC?
[05:15] Jonah: The public SOC 2 covers Redwood hosted offerings. For private/VPC deployments we provide additional documentation; some controls are in your remit if you manage the infra. We'll put together a mapping doc.
[05:30] Miguel: Sounds good. Another item: retention during POC. Our policy is minimum 30 days, max 1 year, but for pilot we usually do 90 days. We need to understand how quickly logs can be purged on request.
[05:45] Jonah: We support on-demand deletion of customer data; for hosted we can run a purge and confirm with an audit token. If you're exporting to your S3, you control retention there.
[05:55] Karen: OK, must have documented purge SLA.
[06:00] Maya: We'll include a short purge procedure and confirmation flow in the docs.
[06:10] Priya: Is there a retention difference for embeddings or KV cache? We worry about cached context in the runtime.
[06:20] Jonah: The KV cache is ephemeral per instance; by default it's not persisted long-term, but we do have prefix cache for performance. We'll detail what's persisted and how to configure TTLs.
[06:35] Miguel: There's been a note in our security review that some labels in earlier docs were mis-typed - 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' - so just standard doc quality thing.
[06:45] (laughter)
[06:50] Maya: Noted, we'll fix typos.
[07:00] Karen: On the legal side, we need to know whether Redwood can sign a data processing addendum and our standard security questionnaire.
[07:10] Maya: Yes, Redwood signs DPAs and we can complete your security questionnaire. I'll follow up with the legal checklist and the DPA template.
[07:20] Karen: For the pilot evidence, can we run a quick technical verification - like a scripted test that demonstrates log export and SSO mapping?
[07:30] Jonah: Absolutely, we can run a smoke test. Proposed workflow: we set up a test tenant, you run a couple of SSO logins, we trigger requests through the API, then export logs to your S3 and confirm mapping.
[07:45] Miguel: We'll need an example log schema to map to our SIEM.
[07:52] Jonah: I'll attach the sample schema and a few sample events.
[08:00] Maya: Timing - can we aim to do the technical verification next week? Miguel, you mentioned a couple of constraints on 7/22?
[08:10] Miguel: I can do 7/23 afternoon, that works.
[08:16] Priya: Works for me.
[08:18] Karen: Quick Q: who has access to the raw prompts during the pilot internally at Redwood?
[08:26] Jonah: Access is role-based. Only engineers with the required RBAC role can access unredacted prompts. We keep an access log for those sessions and can export it.
[08:36] Karen: That's good. We need a list of the roles and associated permissions.
[08:42] Maya: We'll share the RBAC matrix.
[08:45] (brief pause)
[08:52] Miguel: One more - does Redwood support IP allowlisting for API calls from our VPC?
[09:00] Jonah: Yes for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we support IP restrictions via customer-configured egress/VPN or we can provide peered endpoints in some regions.
[09:12] Miguel: We'll probably opt for Private when we move beyond POC.
[09:18] Maya: Totally makes sense.
[09:22] Karen: On SOC 2 evidence, I will send the list of specific controls we need validated; we have a short list around access management, logging, and change control.
[09:32] Maya: Great, send that to me and we'll map the evidence points.
[09:36] Priya: Any blockers on pricing for enabling these features in POC?
[09:42] Maya: No blockers - POC typically covered by credits; if you enable Dedicated or Private we can talk about committed capacity. We'll send a note on cost implications for extended retention and BYOK.
[09:55] Karen: Competitors - we've looked at Anthropic and AWS Bedrock, mostly to compare security posture.
[10:05] Maya: Noted. Our differentiators here are the private deployment path, BYOK, and transparent audit logs.
[10:15] Miguel: Okay, next steps?
[10:18] Maya: I'll summarize now. Action items: I'll send SAML metadata tailored to staging and prod, the DPA template, RBAC matrix. Jonah will send sample audit logs and the log schema. Miguel will confirm retention and S3 ingestion details. Karen will send SOC2 control list. We'll target the technical verification week of 7/22-7/24, tentatively 7/23.
[10:45] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Karen: Thanks.
[10:52] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up by end of week with docs.

End of meeting.
